![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/c62793a0dc7ff37a4d6b7cf157239f21e6b0cdef8c3d428916f074584462598b.png)

The region enclosed by the curves $y={x}^{2}$ and $y=3x$ for $y\in [0,9]$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=5.$ Find the volume of the resulting solid.
question.worked_solution:
First, since we are rotating about a vertical line, we need to solve the equations of our curves for $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{y} \\ y & =3x\,⟹\,x=\frac{1}{3}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/bd75a7448cfda8237a403f4ea67a99c38e41788839f5c88b89487106e49547d3.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x=\sqrt{y},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $x=\frac{1}{3}y.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=\frac{1}{3}y.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/0ec13c4447954916af6e3b72abffefb69a46a12671b7b8388a873835654ec921.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{9}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{9}{[\,(5)-(\frac{1}{3}y)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{9}{[5-\frac{1}{3}y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=\sqrt{y}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/7404d889d1388540821bbd282f82322e3249534b8d4518a6236e9f4bf3164d2c.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{9}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{9}[\,(5)-(\sqrt{y})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{9}[5-\sqrt{y}]^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{9}({(5-\frac{1}{3}y)}^{2}-{(5-\sqrt{y})}^{2})\,\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{9}(\frac{1}{9}{y}^{2}-\frac{13}{3}y+10\sqrt{y})\,\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {(\frac{20{y}^{3/2}}{3}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{27}-\frac{13{y}^{2}}{6})|}_{0}^{9} \\  & =\pi [(\frac{20\cdot {9}^{3/2}}{3}+\frac{{9}^{3}}{27}-\frac{13\cdot {9}^{2}}{6})-0] \\  & =\frac{63\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
